gates.description: All metrics must have a precise definition (name, formula, data source, baseline, target)
Guardrail metrics must be identified to catch unintended degradation
Statistical results must include confidence intervals, not just point estimates
Data quality must be validated before analysis (completeness, freshness, duplicates)
Results must be segmented — aggregate metrics hide the signal
No vanity metrics (cumulative totals, always-increasing counters) as primary success metrics

anti_patterns.description: Tracking 200 metrics and reporting on all of them — if you report everything, you highlight nothing
Reporting metrics that always go up (total registered users, cumulative page views) that never inform a decision
Running an experiment then searching for the metric that shows a positive result — p-hacking
Requesting more data before making a decision when existing data is sufficient — perfect data does not exist
Building dashboards that nobody checks — no clear audience, no clear decision they inform
Analyzing data from a broken instrumentation pipeline and presenting results as fact — garbage in, garbage out

escalation_triggers: Data instrumentation is fundamentally broken and engineering has not prioritized the fix for more than one sprint
A stakeholder is making a high-impact decision that contradicts the data
An A/B test shows a statistically significant negative result on a guardrail metric and PM wants to ship anyway
Data privacy or compliance concerns arise (tracking without consent, PII in analytics)
Two data sources give contradictory answers for the same metric and the discrepancy cannot be resolved
Analytics pipeline has been unreliable for more than 48 hours, affecting reporting and monitoring

input_requirements.description: PRD.md with feature hypotheses and success criteria to measure

output_certifications: All metrics defined precisely (name, formula, data source, baseline, target)
Guardrail metrics identified for all key analyses
Statistical results include confidence intervals, not just point estimates
Data quality validated before analysis (completeness, freshness, duplicates)
Results segmented by meaningful dimensions (no aggregate-only analysis)
Analysis is reproducible (query or code saved)
